title: writeWarningToast branches on `DroppedFieldsEvent.reason` with a binary ternary, so every future reason is labelled "Read-only"
body:
Found while implementing objectstack#6437 (widening `DroppedFieldsEvent.reason`). Filed unassigned — recording only, not claiming.

## Fact

`packages/app-shell/src/providers/writeWarningToast.ts` picks the toast wording with a binary test:

```ts
reason === 'readonly_when'
  ? t('detail.writeStrippedByState', { … "Not editable in this record's current state…" })
  : t('detail.writeStrippedReadonly', { … 'Read-only, so it did not take effect: {{fields}}' })
```

The `else` arm is not "readonly" — it is "everything that is not `readonly_when`". Any reason added server-side lands there and is announced to the user as **read-only**.

## Why this is not caught by types

`packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts` re-exports THE spec type rather than a hand-widened `string` — deliberately, and its comment says why: a consumer-side widening "deletes the only compile-time signal that would tell `AdapterProvider`'s toast wording (which branches on `readonly_when`) that a new reason had appeared."

That reasoning is right and the mechanism does not deliver it. A ternary is not an exhaustive branch, so `tsc` has nothing to complain about when the union grows — the type import is correct and still silent. The framework side of the same seam uses the shape that does work: `service-automation`'s `DROPPED_REASON_LABEL` is a `Record<DroppedFieldsEvent['reason'], string>`, which fails to compile until the new arm is worded.

## Activation

objectstack#6437 adds `primary_key` (a payload `id` the update dispatch ruled is not an identifier, stripped rather than written over the targeted rows' primary key). It reaches this toast through the ordinary REST `droppedFields` response. So the moment `.objectui-sha`'s spec pin moves past that change, a user who triggers the primary-key strip is told the field is read-only — which is false, and points them at a permissions problem that does not exist. That is the same failure objectui#3484 / framework#3794 fixed for `readonly_when`, one reason later.

## Suggested shape

Replace the ternary with an exhaustive map keyed by `DroppedFieldsEvent['reason']` (mirroring `DROPPED_REASON_LABEL`), so a new reason is a compile error here instead of a wrong sentence in front of a user. Wording for `primary_key` is available in objectstack's `crud-nodes.ts` and in the spec `.describe()`.

Related: objectstack#6437, objectstack#3407, objectstack#5126, objectstack#3794, objectui#3484, objectui#3160.
